title: EU-LAC Dialogues and EU-Mercosur & Chile Workshop on Sustainable Food Systems
executive_summary: The EU-Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) Dialogues on Sustainable Food Systems aim to foster strategic partnerships to accelerate the transition to sustainable agriculture and food systems. Supported by the EU's Foreign Policy Instruments and the EU-LAC Policy Dialogue Facility, these dialogues include four sub-regional workshops and a concluding bi-regional conference planned for late 2022. Key workshops involved EU collaboration with Central America, Mercosur countries, and Chile, focusing on shared challenges such as sustainable livestock production, food loss and waste reduction, soil health, and innovation. The dialogues emphasize alignment with the EU Farm to Fork Strategy and global sustainability goals, including the 2030 Agenda and UN Sustainable Development Goals. Participants, including policymakers and private sector representatives, committed to ongoing cooperation, public-private partnerships, and sharing best practices to build resilient, inclusive, and environmentally sustainable food systems amid global challenges like the pandemic and geopolitical tensions.
characteristics: The EU-LAC Dialogues focus on accelerating the transition to sustainable food systems and agricultural production through strategic partnerships and constructive exchanges.

Workshops cover sub-regions including EU-Mercosur and Chile, Central America, and Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, addressing topics like the EU Farm to Fork Strategy, sustainable livestock, pesticide use, and food loss reduction.

The EU-Mercosur and Chile workshop emphasized cooperation on sustainable livestock production, food loss and waste, soil health, and innovation, aligning with the EU Green Deal and Farm to Fork Strategy.

Key stakeholders include EU representatives, Ministries of Agriculture and Environment from Mercosur countries and Chile, and private sector actors, promoting inclusive, participatory approaches aligned with the 2030 Agenda and UN Sustainable Development Goals.
The dialogues aim to foster ongoing collaboration, public-private partnerships, and sharing of best practices to support global food system sustainability and resilience.
practical_applications: Organisation of EU-Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) Dialogues on Sustainable Food Systems, supported by the Foreign Policy Instruments (FPI) and the EU-LAC Policy Dialogue Facility, including four sub-regional workshops and a concluding bi-regional conference.
Conducting sub-regional workshops focused on sustainable agriculture and food systems, such as:
EU-Mercosur and Chile Workshop (May 16-17, 2022) addressing sustainable livestock production, food loss and waste, and soil health and innovation.
EU-Colombia, Ecuador and Peru Workshop (September 28-29, 2022) discussing sustainable use of pesticides and food loss and waste.
EU-Central America Workshop (March 22-23, 2022) covering the EU Farm to Fork Strategy, responsible food business practices, climate actions, soil protection, and reducing food loss and waste.

Engagement of policy makers from the EU, MERCOSUR countries, and Chile, including Ministries of Agriculture and Environment, and private sector representatives, to identify areas of convergence and develop cooperation strategies.
Promotion of public and private partnerships and sharing of good practices to enable the transition to sustainable and resilient food systems globally.
Alignment of national strategies (e.g., Chile’s strategy for inclusive food systems) with international priorities such as the 2030 Agenda and UN Sustainable Development Goals.
Support for the EU-MERCOSUR Free Trade Agreement as part of a bi-regional Association Agreement to enhance cooperation on sustainable food systems.
commitments: Organize a total of four sub-regional workshops on sustainable food systems, concluding with a bi-regional conference expected to take place at the end of 2022.

commitment_details.text: Organize a total of four sub-regional workshops on sustainable food systems, concluding with a bi-regional conference expected to take place at the end of 2022.

kpi_list.kpi_text: These Dialogues are organised with the support of the Foreign Policy Instruments (FPI) and the EU-Lac Policy Dialogue Facility. They will consist of a total of four sub-regional workshops, and concluding with a bi-regional conference expected to take place at the end of 2022.
kpi_list.metric_name: Number of Sub-regional Workshops and Bi-regional Conference
kpi_list.target_description: Organize four sub-regional workshops and one bi-regional conference
kpi_list.measurement_method: Count of completed workshops and conference
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Foreign Policy Instruments (FPI) and EU-Lac Policy Dialogue Facility

kpi_list.kpi_text: Following the principles of the Farm to Fork (F2F) Strategy which is at the heart of the EU Green Deal, the EU is committed to supporting the global transition towards sustainable agri-food systems.
kpi_list.metric_name: Support for Global Transition to Sustainable Agri-food Systems
kpi_list.target_description: Support the global transition towards sustainable agri-food systems following the Farm to Fork Strategy
kpi_list.measurement_method: Implementation and promotion of Farm to Fork Strategy principles in external policies

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Chilean government seeks to promote fair mechanisms focused on the rights of people working in rural areas, in response to issues related to the sustainability of food systems, but also to inclusion.
kpi_list.metric_name: Promotion of Fair Mechanisms for Rural Workers' Rights
kpi_list.target_description: Promote fair mechanisms focused on the rights of rural workers to enhance sustainability and inclusion in food systems
kpi_list.measurement_method: Development and implementation of policies and strategies supporting rural workers' rights

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Ministry of Agriculture is working on a strategy that will actively involve different stakeholders to ensure that it is a robust participatory process, aligned with international priorities for the sector, such as the 2030 Agenda, the UN Sustainable Goals.
kpi_list.metric_name: Development of Participatory Strategy Aligned with 2030 Agenda
kpi_list.target_description: Develop a robust participatory strategy involving stakeholders aligned with the 2030 Agenda and UN Sustainable Development Goals
kpi_list.measurement_method: Strategy development and stakeholder engagement documentation

kpi_list.kpi_text: As a result of the event, the parties agreed to continue the dialogue and work together on the development of public and private partnerships and sharing of good practices, to enable the transition to sustainable and more resilient Food Systems at global level.
kpi_list.metric_name: Development of Public and Private Partnerships for Sustainable Food Systems
kpi_list.target_description: Continue dialogue and develop partnerships and share good practices to enable transition to sustainable and resilient food systems globally
kpi_list.measurement_method: Number and quality of partnerships and documented good practices shared
kpi_list.responsible_entity: EU, MERCOSUR countries, Chile, and private sector partners

kpi_list.kpi_text: The EU and MERCOSUR Free Trade agreement, part of a bi-regional Association Agreement, which is still pending to be signed and ratified.
kpi_list.metric_name: Signing and Ratification of EU-MERCOSUR Free Trade Agreement
kpi_list.target_description: Sign and ratify the EU-MERCOSUR Free Trade Agreement as part of the bi-regional Association Agreement

kpi_list.kpi_text: Substantial progress was made in identifying areas of convergence and defining common characteristics for a dynamic consensus on food systems improvement, as well as shared commitment towards the need to work together on the global transition to Sustainable Food Systems.
kpi_list.metric_name: Consensus Building on Food Systems Improvement
kpi_list.target_description: Identify areas of convergence and define common characteristics for consensus on food systems improvement and shared commitment to global transition
kpi_list.measurement_method: Documentation of consensus and joint commitments from dialogues

kpi_list.kpi_text: The second day focused on key issues on which strategies and cooperation could be developed, namely in the areas of sustainable livestock production, food loss and waste, and Soil health and Innovation.
kpi_list.metric_name: Development of Strategies and Cooperation in Key Food System Areas
kpi_list.target_description: Develop strategies and cooperation in sustainable livestock production, food loss and waste reduction, and soil health and innovation
kpi_list.measurement_method: Strategy documents and cooperation agreements in the specified areas

top_actors.name: European Union
top_actors.justification: The European Union is the central actor throughout the documents, prominently mentioned as the main organizer and driver of the dialogues and workshops on sustainable food systems. It leads key initiatives such as the Farm to Fork Strategy and the EU Green Deal, and its policies and perspectives are repeatedly referenced, highlighting its major influence on the topics discussed and its role in fostering international cooperation.

top_actors.name: Southern Common Market
top_actors.justification: The Southern Common Market (MERCOSUR) is a key regional partner in the dialogues, actively participating alongside the EU and Chile. It is involved in policy discussions, cooperation efforts, and the pending EU-MERCOSUR Free Trade Agreement, making it a crucial actor in shaping sustainable food systems in the Latin America region.

top_actors.name: Government Officials
top_actors.justification: Government officials from the EU, MERCOSUR countries, and Chile play an important role as representatives and decision-makers in the dialogues. Their participation in workshops and policy exchanges, including high-level figures such as Sandra Gallina and Raúl Cano Ricciardi, underscores their influence on the development and implementation of sustainable food system strategies.

top_themes.name: Bi-regional Cooperation
top_themes.justification: The documents focus extensively on cooperation between the EU and Latin American regions (LAC, Mercosur, Chile, Central America) to promote sustainable food systems. This theme is central to the dialogues, workshops, and policy exchanges described, reflecting a strategic commitment to joint action on sustainability, climate change, and food security.

top_themes.name: EU-LAC Digital Alliance
top_themes.justification: Although listed as a detected theme, there is no explicit mention or content related to digital alliances or digital cooperation in the provided texts. The focus is on sustainable food systems and agricultural cooperation rather than digital matters, making this theme marginal or irrelevant in this context.

top_themes.name: Digital Inclusion
top_themes.justification: The documents emphasize inclusion in terms of social and rural stakeholders in food systems, but do not address digital inclusion specifically. Therefore, this theme is not central and has minimal relevance to the main messages and objectives of the dialogues.
